issues.description: Static method for computing a meal's total price is named inconsistently across artifacts. The problem statement (UML) requires a static method calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int (problem_statement.md). The solution's SealSaloon class implements a static method named computeMealCost(Meal): int (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java, line 57). The template Main calls computeMealCost(Meal) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, line 13 in the template), while the solution's Main calls calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, line 13 in the solution). This mismatch of the expected identifier (calculateTotalPrice) and the actual implementation/call sites (computeMealCost) can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may cause grading/tests to fail if names are not unified.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred): rename the implementation and all call sites to calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int to match the UML and problem statement (rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon and update any Main or tests that call it). Option B: if computeMealCost is preferred, update the problem statement/UML to refer to computeMealCost and update the template and solution Main files to call computeMealCost consistently. Ensure tests and example code reference the same name.
